--- title: "04 — Taxonomy vs. function across habitats and the vent environment" date: last-modified format: html: toc: true code-fold: show df-print: paged editor: source --- # Question **Part 1, habitat and field (all units).** Do habitat (vent vs. non-vent) and vent field shape microeukaryotic **taxonomy** more than **expressed function**? Do habitat (vent vs. non-vent) and vent field shape microeukaryotic **taxonomy** more than **expressed function**? **Environmental effects.** PERMANOVA R^2 and PERMDISP for each matrix. Comparison of PERMANOVA R^2 and PERMDISP will help report how each factor structures taxonomy and function. **Taxonomy vs. function (ΔR^2).** A jackknife confidence interval on R²(taxonomy) − R²(function). Evaluate this change and determine if the contributions are significant or not. **Coupling.** Procrustes correlation between the two ordinations. Are samples that are taxnomically similar to one another also functionally similar? **Part 2, the vent environmental gradient (vent units only).** Which vent geochemical variables track taxonomic and functional structure (dbRDA, PCoA + envfit), and which broad functional categories shift along that gradient? # Set up ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} source(if (file.exists("_setup.R")) "_setup.R" else "scripts/_setup.R") long <- load_long_annot() ``` ::: The taxonomic resolution is fixed at rank 4; from `02_taxonomy_grain_ladder.qmd`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} taxon_grain <- 4L # prevalence floor: taxa and KOs must appear in >= 4 libraries min_prev <- 4L ``` ::: # Functions for 04 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # PERMANOVA (marginal R^2, p) + PERMDISP for each contrast on one distance matrix. ## Field-within-vent is tested only when every vent field has >= min_per_field sample units; smaller strata cannot reach p < 0.05 and are skipped. fit_contrasts <- function(d, meta, matrix_label, min_per_field = 3, permutations = 9999, seed = 20260730) { m <- meta[match(labels(d), meta$sample_unit), ] one_test <- function(dd, mm, rhs, term, label) { r <- run_permanova(dd, mm, formula_rhs = rhs, permutations = permutations, seed = seed) tibble::tibble( contrast = label, R2 = r$R2[r$term == term], p = r$p[r$term == term], dispersion_p = betadisper_check(dd, mm[[term]], permutations, seed)$dispersion_p, n_units = nrow(mm) ) } out <- list( one_test(d, m, ~ vent_bin + field, "vent_bin", "Vent vs. non-vent"), one_test(d, m, ~ vent_bin + field, "field", "Vent field (all units)") ) vent_ids <- m$sample_unit[m$vent_bin == "Vent"] vent_meta <- m[match(vent_ids, m$sample_unit), ] if (n_distinct(vent_meta$field) >= 2 && all(table(vent_meta$field) >= min_per_field)) { vent_d <- stats::as.dist(as.matrix(d)[vent_ids, vent_ids]) out <- c(out, list(one_test(vent_d, vent_meta, ~ field, "field", "Vent field (vent units)"))) } bind_rows(out) |> mutate(matrix = matrix_label, .before = 1) } # Delete-one jackknife: ## R²(taxonomy) − R²(function) for each term. delta_r2_jack <- function(d_tax, d_fxn, meta, terms = c("vent_bin", "field"), conf = 0.95) { tax_mat <- as.matrix(d_tax) ids <- rownames(tax_mat) fxn_mat <- as.matrix(d_fxn)[ids, ids] m <- meta[match(ids, meta$sample_unit), ] n <- length(ids) marginal_r2 <- function(full_mat, idx) { fit <- vegan::adonis2(stats::as.dist(full_mat[idx, idx]) ~ vent_bin + field, data = droplevels(m[idx, ]), by = "margin", permutations = 9) # R² only; p unused (vegan needs > 1) fit[terms, "R2"] } draw <- function(idx, dropped) { tibble::tibble(dropped = dropped, term = terms, r2_tax = marginal_r2(tax_mat, idx), r2_fxn = marginal_r2(fxn_mat, idx), delta = r2_tax - r2_fxn) } observed <- draw(seq_len(n), NA_character_) jack <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(n), \(i) draw(seq_len(n)[-i], ids[i])) t_crit <- stats::qt(1 - (1 - conf) / 2, df = n - 1) summary <- jack |> left_join(select(observed, term, delta_observed = delta), by = "term") |> group_by(term) |> summarise( delta_observed = dplyr::first(delta_observed), delta_jack = mean(n * delta_observed - (n - 1) * delta), # bias-corrected ΔR² jack_se = sqrt((n - 1) / n * sum((delta - mean(delta))^2)), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(ci_low = (delta_jack - t_crit * jack_se), ci_high = (delta_jack + t_crit * jack_se)) |> left_join(select(observed, term, r2_tax, r2_fxn), by = "term") |> relocate(term, r2_tax, r2_fxn, delta_observed, delta_jack, jack_se) list(summary = summary, draws = jack) } ``` ::: *Delete one jacknife* Each draw drops one sample unit and refits the marginal PERMANOVA on both matrices. A jackknife never draws a unit twice, so there are no zero-distance duplicate pairs inflating R^2 (the bias in the earlier bootstrap version). rclr is a within-sample transform, so dropping a unit = dropping its row and column of the finished distance matrices; nothing is rebuilt (Efron & Stein 1981). _CI = bias-corrected estimate ± t(n − 1) × jackknife SE_ # Configure Part 2 Establish parameters that are used below ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Select vent fields FIELDS_IN_SCOPE <- c("Gorda Ridge", "Von Damm", "Piccard") # Taxonomic level, 4. See script 02 CHOSEN_DEPTH <- 4 # See how biological units are assigned. UNIT_COL <- "sample_unit" ENV_VARS <- c("TEMP", "pH", "CH4", "Mg") # Model-scale versions (CH4 enters as log10). redundancy determined with temp and CH4, see log10 scale option here. ENV_MODEL_VARS <- c("TEMP", "pH", "log10_CH4", "Mg") # Permutation num N_PERM_MODEL <- 9999 ``` ::: # Part 1: habitat and field structure (all units) ## Definitions - set up for using taxonomic level 4 Same transcripts feed both matrices. Only the column they are summed by changes (`taxon` vs. `ko_id`). Three filters make that true and set the unit of analysis: 1. Shared prep (`prep_paired()`): Gorda Ridge, Von Damm and Piccard only; no per-row TPM cutoff; transcripts need a lineage and a KO, so the same transcripts count toward both taxonomy and function; Eukaryota-only and Opisthokonta lineages are dropped. 2. Taxa and KOs must each appear in at least `min_prev` libraries (`prevalence_filter()`, the 02 decision). Both filters run on the same table in sequence, so a row that fails either one leaves both matrices. 3. Replicate libraries are averaged to their sample unit (`aggregate = "mean"` in `build_matrix()`). Ravelin2, Lotsoshrimp, and Gorda Plume each have two libraries; permuting them as independent samples is pseudoreplication. Every test below runs on sample units. * isolate non-Axial samples * skip TPM subset * check for multiKO ID transcripts * remove opisthokonta ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # shared prep (R/prep_paired.R): 3 fields, no row TPM cutoff, multi-KO split paired <- prep_paired(long, depth = taxon_grain) |> prevalence_filter("taxon", min_samples = min_prev) |> prevalence_filter("ko_id", min_samples = min_prev) # one row per sample unit: the unit of analysis for every test meta <- paired |> dplyr::distinct(sample_unit, field, vent_bin, n_reps) |> dplyr::arrange(sample_unit) # each unit must sit in exactly one field x habitat cell stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(meta$sample_unit) == nrow(meta)) ``` ::: Libraries and sample units per stratum. Report sample units as *n*. Libraries missing here compared with `long` were dropped by the TPM, lineage, or prevalence filters. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} paired |> dplyr::distinct(sample_id, vent_bin, field) |> dplyr::count(vent_bin, field, name = "libraries") |> dplyr::left_join(dplyr::count(meta, vent_bin, field, name = "sample_units"), by = c("vent_bin", "field")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} setdiff(unique(long$sample_id), unique(paired$sample_id)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` character(0) ``` ::: ::: ## Taxonomy and function matrices Robust Aitchison (rclr + Euclidean) matrices from scaled TPM, averaged to sample units. Build matrices for each, taxonomy and function. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tax <- build_matrix(paired, "taxon", min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform, aggregate = "mean", unit_col = "sample_unit") fxn <- build_matrix(paired, "ko_id", min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform, aggregate = "mean", unit_col = "sample_unit") # same sample units, same order, in both matrices and in meta stopifnot(identical(labels(tax$dist), labels(fxn$dist)), setequal(labels(tax$dist), meta$sample_unit)) c(taxonomy_features = ncol(tax$mat), function_features = ncol(fxn$mat), sample_units = nrow(tax$mat)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` taxonomy_features function_features sample_units 220 4508 19 ``` ::: ::: ### 1. Environmental effects on each matrix * `R2` is the fraction of that matrix's variance explained by the term (marginal test). * If `dispersion_p` < 0.05, groups differ in spread as well as in centroid, so R² cannot be read as a pure composition difference (Anderson & Walsh 2013). * `n_units` is the number of sample units. If a vent field has fewer than 3 vent units, the within-vent field test is skipped and that row is absent. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} env_effects <- dplyr::bind_rows( # Taxonomy fit_contrasts(tax$dist, meta, "taxonomy", permutations = params$permutations, seed = params$seed), # Function fit_contrasts(fxn$dist, meta, "function", permutations = params$permutations, seed = params$seed)) |> dplyr::arrange(contrast, matrix) env_effects ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: *Table interpretation (env_effect):* * For the vent vs. non-vent comparison, both the taxonomic and functional profiles separate by habitat. **Therefore there is a true difference in composition between vent and non-vent samples.** * Once habitat is accounted for, vent field has little effect on either matrix. * The vent-units-only field test is not run: Piccard has 2 vent units, below `min_per_field = 3`, so that row is absent by design. Do not report a within-vent field R². * Habitat (or sample type) structures both taxonomy and function. Vent field has less of an impact. ### 2. Is taxonomy structured more than function across the deep-sea vent environment? Here the question gets its significance test. For each term: ΔR² = R²(taxonomy) − R²(function) A 95% interval that excludes 0 means the term explains a significantly larger (Δ > 0) or smaller (Δ < 0) share of taxonomic than functional variation. The interval comes from a delete-one jackknife over sample units (Efron & Stein 1981). Each draw drops one unit and refits both PERMANOVAs. `delta_jack` is the bias-corrected ΔR² and `jack_se` its standard error; the CI is centered on `delta_jack`. Reading notes: - Each R² is a share of *its own* matrix's variance. ΔR² asks which matrix the environment organizes more strongly, not which matrix has more variance. - The two matrices differ in dimensions (grain-4 taxa vs. KOs). The interval captures sampling uncertainty, not that structural difference, so keep the wording at "explains a larger share of variation." - If a term has heterogeneous dispersion in either matrix (see step 1), its ΔR² mixes centroid and spread differences. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # input Aitchison distance matrices. delta <- delta_r2_jack(tax$dist, fxn$dist, meta) delta$summary ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: > For results: habitat or smaple type (vent vs. non-vent) explains a similar share of taxonomic and functional variation, and vent field structures neither profile. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} delta$summary |> mutate(term = dplyr::recode(term, vent_bin = "Vent vs. non-vent", field = "Vent field")) |> ggplot(aes(x = delta_observed, y = term)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey40") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high), width = 0.15, color = "#b74a70") + geom_point(size = 3, color = "#b74a70") + labs(x = expression(Delta*R^2~"(taxonomy − function), 95% jackknife CI"), y = NULL) + theme_classic(base_size = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](04_taxonomy_vs_function_files/figure-html/delta-r2-plot-1.png){width=480} ::: ::: ### 3. Are taxonomy and function coupled? (Procrustes) Both ordinations are superimposed and the correlation *r* (0–1) is tested by permutation (Peres-Neto & Jackson 2001). The number of axes is a choice, so we report *r* at 2–4 axes, along with how much of each matrix's variation those axes hold. _High *r* means sample units that are taxonomically similar are also functionally similar._ Caveat: both matrices come from the same transcripts, so some shared structure is built in. That makes *r* an upper bound on biological coupling. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} var_captured <- function(d, k) { eig <- stats::cmdscale(d, k = attr(d, "Size") - 1, eig = TRUE)$eig eig <- eig[eig > 0] sum(eig[seq_len(k)]) / sum(eig) } coupling <- purrr::map_dfr(2:4, \(k) { pt <- procrustes_test(tax$dist, fxn$dist, k = k, permutations = params$permutations, seed = params$seed) tibble::tibble(k_axes = k, procrustes_r= pt$t0, p = pt$signif, tax_var_captured = var_captured(tax$dist, k), fxn_var_captured = var_captured(fxn$dist, k)) }) coupling ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: > For results — Procrustes *r*, *p* and variance captured at k = 2–4 from `04_procrustes.csv`. #### 3b. Is coupling more than a shared response to habitat? Procrustes *r* is highest on the first two axes and falls as axes are added. Those leading axes likely carry the vent/non-vent split, so high *r* could mean only that both matrices separate by habitat. Two checks remove habitat from the comparison: * **Vent units only.** Within one habitat, habitat cannot drive the match. * **Habitat removed.** Each unit's rclr profile is centered on its habitat mean before distances are computed. This is the Euclidean equivalent of partialling `vent_bin` out of a dbRDA on the robust Aitchison distance (Legendre & Anderson 1999). Reading notes: - If *r* stays high and significant in both checks, taxonomy and function are coupled beyond their shared habitat response. - If *r* drops toward the permutation null, the coupling in step 3 is the habitat signal seen twice. - The vent-only test has fewer units, so its *p* is less powerful; compare *r* values, not just significance. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Procrustes r at k axes for one pair of distance matrices (one row per k) coupling_at_k <- function(d_tax, d_fxn, test_label, ks = 2:4) { purrr::map_dfr(ks, \(k) { pt <- procrustes_test(d_tax, d_fxn, k = k, permutations = params$permutations, seed = params$seed) tibble::tibble(test = test_label, k_axes = k, procrustes_r = pt$t0, p = pt$signif, n_units = attr(d_tax, "Size")) }) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # (a) vent units only vent_units <- meta |> dplyr::filter(vent_bin == "Vent") |> dplyr::pull(sample_unit) vent_dist <- function(d) stats::as.dist(as.matrix(d)[vent_units, vent_units]) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # (b) habitat removed: subtract each habitat's mean rclr profile, then Euclidean habitat_removed_dist <- function(mat) { z <- rclr_transform(mat) habitat <- meta$vent_bin[match(rownames(z), meta$sample_unit)] z_resid <- z - apply(z, 2, \(col) stats::ave(col, habitat)) stats::dist(z_resid) } coupling_check <- dplyr::bind_rows( coupling |> dplyr::transmute(test = "All units", k_axes, procrustes_r, p, n_units = attr(tax$dist, "Size")), coupling_at_k(vent_dist(tax$dist), vent_dist(fxn$dist), "Vent units only"), coupling_at_k(habitat_removed_dist(tax$mat), habitat_removed_dist(fxn$mat), "Habitat removed") ) coupling_check ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: > R procrustes value is higher within vent only units, and then when habitat is taken out of the equation, the higher is with all axes. This shows that samples that are taxonomic similar are also functionally similar. *coupled* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} coupling_check |> ggplot(aes(x = k_axes, y = procrustes_r, color = test)) + geom_line() + geom_point(aes(shape = p < 0.05), size = 3) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1), name = "p < 0.05") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:4) + labs(x = "PCoA axes compared", y = "Procrustes r", color = NULL) + theme_classic(base_size = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](04_taxonomy_vs_function_files/figure-html/procrustes-habitat-plot-1.png){width=384} ::: ::: ## Save outputs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} readr::write_csv(env_effects, "output-tables/04_env_effects.csv") readr::write_csv(delta$summary, "output-tables/04_delta_r2.csv") readr::write_csv(coupling, "output-tables/04_procrustes.csv") ``` ::: ## QC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} stopifnot( nrow(meta) == attr(tax$dist, "Size"), # one metadata row per sample unit dplyr::n_distinct(meta$sample_unit) == nrow(meta), # no duplicated units all(c("Vent", "Non-vent") %in% meta$vent_bin), # both habitats present all(c("taxonomy", "function") %in% env_effects$matrix), # both matrices tested nrow(delta$draws) == nrow(meta) * 2, # every jackknife draw completed (2 terms) all(coupling$procrustes_r >= 0 & coupling$procrustes_r <= 1), # >SKH: shared prep rule held (2026-09-25) all(unique(paired$field) %in% c("Gorda Ridge", "Von Damm", "Piccard")), !any(grepl("Opisthokonta", paired$full_classification)) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} readr::write_csv(coupling_check, "output-tables/04_procrustes_habitat_check.csv") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} stopifnot( setequal(unique(coupling_check$test), c("All units", "Vent units only", "Habitat removed")), # all three tests ran all(coupling_check$procrustes_r >= 0 & coupling_check$procrustes_r <= 1), all(coupling_check$n_units[coupling_check$test == "Vent units only"] == length(vent_units)) # vent subset size ) ``` ::: # Part 2: environmental drivers at vents (vent units only) ## Generate tables ### Shared tables - fields in scope, multi-KO split, grain-4 taxon Pre-process data for use. Same input as 02, 04 and 06 (`R/prep_paired.R`): Gorda Ridge, Von Damm and Piccard; transcripts need a taxa and KO assignment. No per-row TPM cutoff; multi-KO transcripts split with TPM divided equally. Remove Eukaryota-only and Opisthokonta lineages. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} paired_mod <- load_paired(fields = FIELDS_IN_SCOPE, depth = CHOSEN_DEPTH) # built at the end of 02 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` [load_paired] data/processed/paired_L4.RData (built 2026-10-23 09:06; 318,911 rows) ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # CHECK STATS n_distinct(paired_mod$sample_id) # Number of libraries ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 21 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} n_distinct(paired_mod[[UNIT_COL]]) # Number of biological units ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 19 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Using taxon level 4. n_distinct(paired_mod$taxon) # unique taxa ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 252 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} n_distinct(paired_mod$ko_id) # unique KOs ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 7643 ``` ::: ::: ### Collapse to biological units Use `unit tables` to establish one row per unit (field, sample tyoe, and number of replicates), ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unit_design <- paired_mod |> distinct(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], field, vent_bin, n_reps) stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unit_design$unit)) n_units <- nrow(unit_design) n_vent <- sum(unit_design$vent_bin == "Vent") n_nonvent <- sum(unit_design$vent_bin == "Non-vent") unit_design |> count(field, vent_bin) |> print(n = Inf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 field vent_bin n 1 Gorda Ridge Non-vent 2 2 Gorda Ridge Vent 4 3 Piccard Non-vent 2 4 Piccard Vent 2 5 Von Damm Non-vent 2 6 Von Damm Vent 7 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} message(glue::glue("{n_units} units ({n_vent} vent, {n_nonvent} non-vent).")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 19 units (13 vent, 6 non-vent). ``` ::: ::: ## Which taxonomic and functional profiles track with the vent environment? Vent units only (13). Non-vent units lack most geochemistry measurements, so they are excluded. **Whole community only.** Does environment structure the taxonomic profile, the KO functional profile, or both? 1. **Constrained.** Distance-based RDA (dbRDA) on robust Aitchison distance (Legendre & Anderson 1999, *Ecol Monogr* 69:1–24), with collinear predictors pruned by VIF and the rest forward-selected only when the global model is significant (Blanchet, Legendre & Borcard 2008, *Ecology* 89:2623–2632). 2. **Unconstrained.** PCoA of the same distances with environmental vectors fitted afterwards (`envfit`), so the axis percentages describe total among-vent variation and cannot overstate how much of the community the environment explains. 3. **Functional investment.** Having established that environment structures the community, which broad functional categories shift with it? Using COG functional categories, KEGG categories, and pfam IDs. > Methane measurement was super different between Von Damm and other vent fields. So it is its own vent field indicator. Needed to partition this out (`condition(field)`) where appropriate to separate the impact. ### Get one environmental parameter row per vent unit From `sample_meta` (`config/sample_metadata.csv`), combine environmental parameters and average duplicates. When tehre are two values, these are averaged (Lotsoshrimp, Ravelin2). For missing values, using an impute approach, where a measurement from the same field and sample type will be used in place of an NA. Likely averaged across similar samples. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} env_vent <- sample_meta |> filter(habitat == "Vent", raw_label %in% unit_design$unit) |> # Vents only group_by(unit = raw_label, field) |> summarise(across(dplyr::all_of(ENV_VARS), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), n_meta_rows = n(), .groups = "drop") |> # mean an all-NA vector is NaN - change to NA mutate(across(dplyr::all_of(ENV_VARS), \(x) if_else(is.nan(x), NA_real_, x))) # stopifnot(nrow(env_vent) == n_vent) # DUP CHECK # Flag first, then fill with the same-field vent mean. ## Add imputed values env_vent <- env_vent |> mutate(across(dplyr::all_of(ENV_VARS), is.na, .names = "{.col}_imputed")) |> group_by(field) |> mutate(across(dplyr::all_of(ENV_VARS), \(x) dplyr::coalesce(x, mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))) |> ungroup() env_vent |> filter(if_any(ends_with("_imputed"))) |> select(unit, field, ends_with("_imputed")) |> print() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 6 unit field TEMP_imputed pH_imputed CH4_imputed Mg_imputed 1 Gorda Ridge_Vent_SirVent… Gord… FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} env_vent |> arrange(field, unit) |> select(unit, field, all_of(ENV_VARS), n_meta_rows) |> print(n = Inf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 13 × 7 unit field TEMP pH CH4 Mg n_meta_rows 1 Gorda Ridge_Vent_Candelabra Gorda Rid… 79 5.5 23.7 36.5 1 2 Gorda Ridge_Vent_MtEdwards Gorda Rid… 40 6 10.1 43.6 1 3 Gorda Ridge_Vent_SirVentsAlot Gorda Rid… 72 5.97 11.6 52 1 4 Gorda Ridge_Vent_VentiLatte Gorda Rid… 11 6.4 0.9 52.1 1 5 Piccard_Vent_Lotsoshrimp Piccard 27.5 6.12 11.7 52.2 2 6 Piccard_Vent_Shrimpocalypse Piccard 85 5.11 27.5 43.9 1 7 Von Damm_Vent_ArrowLoop Von Damm 137 5.69 1894. 18.1 1 8 Von Damm_Vent_Bartizan Von Damm 129 5.8 1617. 22.7 1 9 Von Damm_Vent_OldManTree Von Damm 122. 5.69 1986. 13.7 1 10 Von Damm_Vent_Ravelin2 Von Damm 96.1 5.81 1894. 18 2 11 Von Damm_Vent_ShrimpHole Von Damm 21 7.72 218. 51.8 1 12 Von Damm_Vent_WhiteCastle Von Damm 108 5.49 2252. 8.9 1 13 Von Damm_Vent_X18 Von Damm 48 6.99 1310. 28 1 ``` ::: ::: ### Transform data, check collinearity, standardize across parameters CH4 spans three orders of magnitude and enters as log10. Everything is z-scored centered/normalized. Assuming Variane inflation factor (VIF) is 10; this will help us figure out how the variance of an estimated regression increases because of collinearity. When two variables are linearly related, it can cuase issues inflating results, etc. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} env_model <- env_vent |> mutate(log10_CH4 = log10(CH4)) |> select(unit, field, dplyr::all_of(ENV_MODEL_VARS)) |> mutate(across(dplyr::all_of(ENV_MODEL_VARS), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x)))) # Pairwise correlation among candidates: expect TEMP and Mg to be tightly (negatively) coupled, because both index the fraction of vent fluid in the sample. stats::cor(env_model[ENV_MODEL_VARS], method = "spearman") |> round(2) |> print() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` TEMP pH log10_CH4 Mg TEMP 1.00 -0.74 0.77 -0.80 pH -0.74 1.00 -0.45 0.53 log10_CH4 0.77 -0.45 1.00 -0.89 Mg -0.80 0.53 -0.89 1.00 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} env_keep <- vif_select(env_model[ENV_MODEL_VARS], thresh = 10) message(glue::glue("Retained after VIF < 10: {paste(env_keep, collapse = ', ')}")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Retained after VIF < 10: TEMP, pH, Mg ``` ::: ::: > Retained after VIF < 10: TEMP, pH, Mg. `vif` application is code that will remove environmental predictors that are redundant in the downstream dbRDA. Considers the `Variance inflation factor`. Collinear predictors were removed by iteratively dropping the variable with the highest variance inflation factor until all VIFs were < 10 (Dormann et al. 2013); the retained variables were then forward-selected (Blanchet et al. 2008). *Even after scaling we need to drop the CH4* ### Subset vent-only community matrices Same builder and prevalence filter as 02/04 (features in >= 4 libraries), restricted to vent libraries, averaged to biological units. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vent_long <- paired_mod |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent") q1_levels <- c(taxonomy = "taxon", ko = "ko_id") q1_mats <- purrr::map(q1_levels, \(feat) build_matrix(prevalence_filter(vent_long, feat, 4), feat, min_tpm = 0, aggregate = "mean", unit_col = UNIT_COL)) purrr::iwalk(q1_mats, \(m, lvl) message(glue::glue( "{lvl}: {nrow(m$mat)} units x {ncol(m$mat)} features"))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` taxonomy: 13 units x 179 features ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ko: 13 units x 2742 features ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # stopifnot(purrr::map_lgl(q1_mats, \(m) setequal(labels(m$dist), env_model$unit))) ``` ::: ### Run dbRDA *Does environment structure taxonomy, function, or both?* For each level, the full model parameters that passed collinearity test, its global test, forward selection (only if the global test passes), and a per-variable table with and without field partialled out. Constrained ordination (dbRDA) using robust Aitchison distance. This will model the impact of an explanatory matrix (environemtal factors) on a dependent (or response) matrix (TPM results). Oridinate matrix *Y* (which is the TPM results, the community response) to see what ordination axes are linear combinations of those from *X* (environmental matrix). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit_env_dbrda <- function(d, env, vars, n_perm = N_PERM_MODEL) { env <- env[match(labels(d), env$unit), ] stopifnot(identical(env$unit, labels(d))) # Set up dbRDAs ## Uses temp, pH and Mg, full model full <- vegan::dbrda(stats::reformulate(vars, response = "d"), data = env) ## establish start point for forward selection model null <- vegan::dbrda(d ~ 1, data = env) ## permuration test, rows via n_perm. If p < 0.05, forward selection will run. global <- vegan::anova.cca(full, permutations = n_perm) # ## If the full model using temp, pH, and Mg is significant, then a global model will be run. Otherwise, fall back. sel <- if (global$`Pr(>F)`[1] <= 0.05) { vegan::ordiR2step(null, scope = stats::formula(full), R2scope = TRUE, permutations = n_perm, trace = FALSE) } else null selected <- setdiff(all.vars(stats::formula(sel)), "d") # Blanchet's second stopping rule rejects any step when adj R2 exceeds the global model. ## Only 1 may be returned, so selection returns nothing even though the global test passed. If significant, it is significant. use that. best_single <- NA_character_ if (global$`Pr(>F)`[1] <= 0.05 && length(selected) == 0) { single_r2 <- purrr::map_dbl(vars, \(v) vegan::RsquareAdj( vegan::dbrda(stats::reformulate(v, response = "d"), data = env))$adj.r.squared) best_single <- vars[which.max(single_r2)] best_model <- vegan::dbrda(stats::reformulate(best_single, response = "d"), data = env) if (vegan::anova.cca(best_model, permutations = n_perm)$`Pr(>F)`[1] <= 0.05) { sel <- best_model; selected <- best_single message(glue::glue(" {best_single} alone (adj R2 = {round(max(single_r2), 3)}) ", "exceeds the global model; kept as the single selected variable.")) } } # Each variable alone, then the same variable after removing field. per_var <- purrr::map_dfr(vars, function(v) { alone <- vegan::dbrda(stats::reformulate(v, response = "d"), data = env) cond <- vegan::dbrda(stats::as.formula(paste("d ~", v, "+ Condition(field)")), data = env) tibble::tibble( variable = v, adjR2_alone = vegan::RsquareAdj(alone)$adj.r.squared, p_alone= vegan::anova.cca(alone, permutations = n_perm)$`Pr(>F)`[1], adjR2_given_field = vegan::RsquareAdj(cond)$adj.r.squared, p_given_field = vegan::anova.cca(cond, permutations = n_perm)$`Pr(>F)`[1]) }) list(full = full, selected_model = sel, selected = selected, global_F = global$F[1], global_p = global$`Pr(>F)`[1], full_adjR2 = vegan::RsquareAdj(full)$adj.r.squared, per_var = per_var) } ``` ::: Above function will run the global test, forward selection, and find (if necessary) the best single variable with and without vent field considered. Run dbRDA ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(params$seed) # Run RDA for all community matrices and short output ## Use map to loop over the matrices, "\(m)" will loop through one element at a time. q1_fits <- purrr::map(q1_mats, \(m) fit_env_dbrda(m$dist, env_model, env_keep)) # compare taxonomy vs function, same units, same predictors q1_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(q1_fits, \(f, lvl) tibble::tibble( level = lvl, full_adjR2 = round(f$full_adjR2, 3), global_F = round(f$global_F, 2), global_p= f$global_p, selected = if (length(f$selected)) paste(f$selected, collapse = " + ") else "none")) q1_summary |> print() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 level full_adjR2 global_F global_p selected 1 taxonomy 0.082 1.36 0.0076 TEMP 2 ko 0.042 1.17 0.109 none ``` ::: ::: > Table represents community level dbRDA results, across 13 vent ssites. Temperature stands out as the most important parameter. Temperature was the forward selected parameter too, once pH and Mg were added it did not change the outcome. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} q1_per_var <- purrr::imap_dfr(q1_fits, \(f, lvl) dplyr::mutate(f$per_var, level = lvl)) |> relocate(level) |> mutate(across(starts_with("adjR2"), \(x) round(x, 3))) q1_per_var |> print(n = Inf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 6 level variable adjR2_alone p_alone adjR2_given_field p_given_field 1 taxonomy TEMP 0.054 0.0067 0.075 0.004 2 taxonomy pH 0.026 0.112 0.037 0.103 3 taxonomy Mg 0.011 0.217 0.012 0.254 4 ko TEMP 0.035 0.0202 0.068 0.0016 5 ko pH 0.037 0.0792 0.061 0.0172 6 ko Mg 0.013 0.172 0.038 0.0322 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Unconstrained PCoA of the full vent-only distance matrix, with environmentalvariables fitted afterwards (envfit). Unlike the dbRDA biplot, the axes show % of TOTAL among-vent variation, so the figure cannot overstate how muchof the community the environment explains. # All ENV_MODEL_VARS are fitted (collinearity does not matter here: each vector is fitted on its own) ##Two p-values per vector: ### p_free-units permuted freely across all 13 vents ###p_within_field-units permuted only within their field, so a vector that merely separates fields does not look significant. q1_pcoa <- purrr::imap(q1_mats, function(m, lvl) { pc<- stats::cmdscale(m$dist, k = 2, eig = TRUE) eig <- pc$eig[pc$eig > 0] pct <- round(100 * eig[1:2] / sum(eig), 1) env <- env_model[match(labels(m$dist), env_model$unit), ] stopifnot(identical(env$unit, labels(m$dist))) env_mat <- as.data.frame(env[ENV_MODEL_VARS]) fit_free<- vegan::envfit(pc$points, env_mat, permutations = N_PERM_MODEL) fit_block <- vegan::envfit(pc$points, env_mat, permutations = permute::how(blocks = factor(env$field), nperm = N_PERM_MODEL)) # Get data to work with, vectors, then sites vectors <- tibble::tibble( variable= ENV_MODEL_VARS, dir1 = fit_free$vectors$arrows[, 1], dir2 = fit_free$vectors$arrows[, 2], r2 = unname(fit_free$vectors$r), p_free = unname(fit_free$vectors$pvals), p_within_field = unname(fit_block$vectors$pvals)) |> mutate(level = lvl, .before = 1) #sites sites <- tibble::tibble(unit = labels(m$dist), ax1 = pc$points[, 1], ax2 = pc$points[, 2]) |> left_join(select(env_vent, unit, field, TEMP), by = "unit") list(sites = sites, vectors = vectors, pct = pct) }) q1_envfit <- purrr::map_dfr(q1_pcoa, "vectors") |> mutate(across(c(r2, dir1, dir2), \(x) round(x, 3))) q1_envfit |> select(-dir1, -dir2) |> print(n = Inf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 8 × 5 level variable r2 p_free p_within_field 1 taxonomy TEMP 0.5 0.0217 0.0079 2 taxonomy pH 0.254 0.228 0.0447 3 taxonomy log10_CH4 0.182 0.380 0.533 4 taxonomy Mg 0.126 0.532 0.481 5 ko TEMP 0.455 0.0423 0.0165 6 ko pH 0.353 0.118 0.0117 7 ko log10_CH4 0.147 0.466 0.502 8 ko Mg 0.278 0.201 0.0397 ``` ::: ::: For each variable listed, `env fit` table shows how it matches withthe first 2 PCoA axes. R^2 value of 0.537 for temperature means that vent protist taxonomic assignment predicts about half of the temperature differences. Also for taxa, pH is only significant within vents only. CH4 and Mg don't line up with the 2 main PCoA axes. For the functional profiles, temperature is also strongest, but p-value (free-permuration) undermines this. The functional expression varied similarly to the taxonomic gradient with temperature, but had a broader environmental signature. Once the individual vent differences are taken into account, more is significant. Together, this shows that temperature, acidity and Mg form a gradient for both taxonomy and function. #### Plot PCoA Axes with percentage of total among vent variation, color by temperature, solid arrows are significant. Arrow length = sqrt(r2), scaled to the point cloud: a long arrow means the variable is well aligned with the first two axes, not that it is important in the full community. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} q1_pcoa_plots <- purrr::imap(q1_pcoa, function(p, lvl) { reach <- 0.9 * max(abs(c(p$sites$ax1, p$sites$ax2))) arrows <- p$vectors |> mutate(xend = dir1 * sqrt(r2) * reach, yend = dir2 * sqrt(r2) * reach, sig = p_within_field <= 0.05, label = glue::glue("{variable} (r2 = {round(r2, 2)})")) # Plot ggplot(p$sites, aes(ax1, ax2)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.2, colour = "grey75") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.2, colour = "grey75") + geom_point(aes(fill = TEMP, shape = field), size = 3, colour = "grey20") + geom_segment(data = arrows, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = xend, yend = yend, linetype = sig), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) + geom_text(data = arrows, aes(x = xend * 1.15, y = yend * 1.15, label = label), size = 2.8) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 24), name = NULL) + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Temp (°C)") + scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "solid", `FALSE` = "dashed"), labels = c(`TRUE` = "p <= 0.05", `FALSE` = "n.s."), name = "envfit\n(within field)", drop = FALSE) + # scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.3)) + # scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) + coord_equal(clip = "off") + labs(x = glue::glue("PCoA 1 ({p$pct[1]}%)"), y = glue::glue("PCoA 2 ({p$pct[2]}%)"), title = if (lvl == "ko") "Function" else "Taxonomy") + theme_bw(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) }) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} patchwork::wrap_plots(q1_pcoa_plots, nrow = 1, guides = "collect") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](04_taxonomy_vs_function_files/figure-html/q1-pcoa-plot-save-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # ggsave("figures/pcoa-plot-supp.svg", width = 8, height = 6, device = "svg", limitsize = FALSE) ``` ::: Temperature continues to be the main environmental variable assocaited with protist taxonomic composition and distribution. Across the vent sites samples, temperature explained 5.5% of the variation and this remained with and without vent field considered. pH and Mg (CH4 was found to be redundant) did not add any major explanatory variables. When the same analysis was run with functional profiles, tmperature explained only 3.5% of the variation of kegg annotated transcripts, pH was 3.7%, and Mg was 1.3% (lower). All these of the environmental parameters considered were significant when vent field was considered. Performs unconstrained ordinates (x2) for the vent sites. Temperature was the environmental variable most closely aligned with the taxonomic and functional variations across the data. ### Sensitivity: drop the imputed vent unit Gorda SirVentsAlot has no measured pH or CH4; both were filled with the Gorda vent mean. Refit the community dbRDA without that unit (12 vent units). If the per-variable results hold, the imputation is not driving them. Predictors are not re-scaled, because dbRDA fit statistics do not change under linear rescaling of a predictor. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} imputed_units <- env_vent |> filter(dplyr::if_any(ends_with("_imputed"))) |> pull(unit) set.seed(params$seed) q1_per_var_no_imputed <- purrr::imap_dfr(q1_mats, function(m, lvl) { keep <- setdiff(labels(m$dist), imputed_units) d <- stats::as.dist(as.matrix(m$dist)[keep, keep]) # Run dbRDA fit_env_dbrda(d, filter(env_model, unit %in% keep), env_keep)$per_var |> mutate(level = lvl, n_units = length(keep), .before = 1) }) q1_imputation_check <- q1_per_var |> select(level, variable, adjR2_alone, p_alone) |> left_join(q1_per_var_no_imputed |> select(level, variable, n_units, adjR2_alone_no_imputed = adjR2_alone, p_alone_no_imputed = p_alone), by = c("level", "variable")) |> mutate(across(starts_with("adjR2"), \(x) round(x, 3))) message(glue::glue("Imputed unit(s) dropped: {paste(imputed_units, collapse = ', ')}")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Imputed unit(s) dropped: Gorda Ridge_Vent_SirVentsAlot ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} q1_imputation_check ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Environmental parameters readr::write_csv(env_vent, "output-tables/04_q1_env_vent.csv") readr::write_csv(q1_summary,"output-tables/04_q1_dbrda_summary.csv") readr::write_csv(q1_per_var,"output-tables/04_q1_dbrda_per_variable.csv") readr::write_csv(q1_envfit,"output-tables/04_q1_pcoa_envfit.csv") # Sensitivity check on the imputed vent unit. readr::write_csv(q1_imputation_check, "output-tables/04_q1_imputation_sensitivity.csv") ``` ::: ## Functional category composition along the vent gradient *Which functional categories shift in share of expression along the vent gradient?* Each COG category's rclr share across the 13 vent units is rank-correlated (Spearman, permutation p) with each retained environmental variable, and all category x variable tests are BH-corrected as one family. The same scan on KEGG BRITE level-B categories, an independent annotation of the same transcripts, is the check on any COG hit. One association clears BH: **amino acid transport and metabolism (COG E) takes a larger share of expression at higher temperature**, and KEGG Amino acid metabolism moves the same way. Temperature, Mg and pH all trace the hydrothermal fluid fraction, so the weaker E correlations with Mg and pH are the same signal, not separate results. With 13 units this is exploratory, and "larger share" means a larger fraction of expression, not more transcripts per cell. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # COG functional categories (Galperin et al. 2021, Nucleic Acids Res 49:D274-D281). Single letters, as eggNOG-mapper emits them. COG_DESCRIPTIONS <- c( J = "Translation, ribosomal structure and biogenesis", A = "RNA processing and modification", K = "Transcription", L = "Replication, recombination and repair", B = "Chromatin structure and dynamics", D = "Cell cycle control, cell division, chromosome partitioning", Y = "Nuclear structure", V = "Defense mechanisms", T = "Signal transduction mechanisms", M = "Cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis", N = "Cell motility", Z = "Cytoskeleton", W = "Extracellular structures", U = "Intracellular trafficking, secretion, vesicular transport", O = "Post-translational modification, protein turnover, chaperones", X = "Mobilome: prophages, transposons", C = "Energy production and conversion", G = "Carbohydrate transport and metabolism", E = "Amino acid transport and metabolism", F = "Nucleotide transport and metabolism", H = "Coenzyme transport and metabolism", I = "Lipid transport and metabolism", P = "Inorganic ion transport and metabolism", Q = "Secondary metabolites biosynthesis, transport, catabolism", R = "General function prediction only", S = "Function unknown") N_PERM_CAT <- 9999 # permutations per correlation # KO -> KEGG BRITE level B; animal-centric classes (Organismal Systems, Human Diseases) and non-pathways removed KEGG_BRITE_FILE <- "data/external/ko00001.keg" KEGG_EXCLUDE_A <- c("09150", "09160", "09180", "09190") # The reported result and its KEGG counterpart FOCUS_VAR <- "TEMP" FOCUS_COG <- "E" # Amino acid transport and metabolism FOCUS_KEGG <- "09105" # Amino acid metabolism sig_color <- "#346D6E" # _brand.yml deep-teal ``` ::: Spearman rho per category against one variable. The p-value shuffles the variable across units, so the null keeps each category's own distribution and only breaks its link to the variable. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} spearman_perm <- function(z, x, n_perm = N_PERM_CAT) { stopifnot(nrow(z) == length(x)) # a category with the same value in every unit has no ranks to correlate keep <- apply(z, 2, \(col) stats::sd(col) > 0) if (any(!keep)) { message(glue::glue(" dropped {sum(!keep)} zero-variance feature(s): ", "{paste(colnames(z)[!keep], collapse = ', ')}")) } z <- z[, keep, drop = FALSE] if (ncol(z) == 0) stop("No variable features left to correlate.", call. = FALSE) rz <- scale(apply(z, 2, rank)) rx <- as.numeric(scale(rank(x))) n <- length(x) rho <- as.vector(crossprod(rz, rx)) / (n - 1) perm <- replicate(n_perm, sample(rx)) # units x n_perm null <- abs(crossprod(rz, perm)) / (n - 1) # features x n_perm tibble::tibble(feature = colnames(z), rho = rho, p_perm = (1 + rowSums(null >= abs(rho))) / (1 + n_perm)) } ``` ::: ### COG scan A transcript with several COG letters (e.g. `"BDLTU"`) splits its scaledTPM equally across them. Categories are summed per biological unit (`sum / n_reps`) and the units x category matrix is rclr-transformed. All 26 categories are kept, including `R` and `S`, because the CLR reference needs the whole composition. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (!"COG_category" %in% names(paired_mod)) { stop("`COG_category` is not in the annotation table. This section needs the eggNOG ", "COG column carried from long_frenemies_annot_tax.", call. = FALSE) } # transcript id for the support counts; fall back to counting rows TX_ID <- c("SEQ_ID", "SequenceID")[c("SEQ_ID", "SequenceID") %in% names(paired_mod)][1] cog_split <- paired_mod |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent", !is.na(COG_category), !COG_category %in% c("", "-")) |> mutate(.txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else row_number(), n_cog = nchar(COG_category)) |> separate_longer_position(COG_category, width = 1) |> rename(cog = COG_category) |> mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cog) cog_mat <- cog_split |> group_by(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], n_reps, cog) |> summarise(tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / first(n_reps), .groups = "drop") |> select(-n_reps) |> pivot_wider(names_from = cog, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |> tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |> as.matrix() cog_mat <- cog_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE] # align rows to the dbRDA predictors cog_z <- rclr_transform(cog_mat) cog_support <- cog_split |> summarise(n_transcripts = n_distinct(.txid), n_kos = n_distinct(ko_id), total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM), .by = cog) |> mutate(pct_tpm = round(100 * total_tpm / sum(total_tpm), 2), description = unname(COG_DESCRIPTIONS[cog])) |> arrange(desc(total_tpm)) set.seed(params$seed) cog_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v) spearman_perm(cog_z, env_model[[v]]) |> mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |> rename(cog = feature) |> mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")) |> # one family: every category x variable left_join(select(cog_support, cog, description, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm), by = "cog") |> mutate(direction = if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"), significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |> arrange(q_bh) message(glue::glue("{nrow(cog_mat)} vent units x {ncol(cog_mat)} COG categories; ", "{sum(cog_gradient$significant)} of {nrow(cog_gradient)} tests clear BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 13 vent units x 24 COG categories; 1 of 72 tests clear BH q <= 0.05 ``` ::: ::: ### KEGG check Same build with KEGG BRITE level-B categories. A KO in *n* level-B categories splits its scaledTPM equally across them; KOs with no retained category drop out, so the composition is over mapped expression only. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (!file.exists(KEGG_BRITE_FILE)) { stop("`", KEGG_BRITE_FILE, "` not found. Download the KEGG BRITE KO hierarchy once, e.g.\n", " curl -o ", KEGG_BRITE_FILE, " \"https://rest.kegg.jp/get/br:ko00001\"\n", "then re-run.", call. = FALSE) } # >SKH: shared parser R/read_brite.R (same map 05, 05b and 06 use; 2026-10-12) brite_map <- read_brite_level_b(KEGG_BRITE_FILE, exclude_a = KEGG_EXCLUDE_A) |> select(ko_id, kegg_a, kegg, description, n_cat) kegg_split <- paired_mod |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent") |> transmute(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], n_reps, ko_id, scaledTPM, .txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else row_number()) |> inner_join(brite_map, by = "ko_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |> mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cat) # mass conservation: splitting across categories must not create or lose TPM vent_ko_tpm <- paired_mod |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent") mapped_tpm <- sum(vent_ko_tpm$scaledTPM[vent_ko_tpm$ko_id %in% brite_map$ko_id]) stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(kegg_split$scaledTPM), mapped_tpm))) kegg_mat <- kegg_split |> summarise(tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / first(n_reps), .by = c(unit, n_reps, kegg)) |> select(-n_reps) |> pivot_wider(names_from = kegg, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |> tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |> as.matrix() kegg_mat <- kegg_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE] kegg_z <- rclr_transform(kegg_mat) kegg_support <- kegg_split |> summarise(n_transcripts = n_distinct(.txid), n_kos = n_distinct(ko_id), total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM), .by = c(kegg, description)) |> mutate(pct_tpm = round(100 * total_tpm / sum(total_tpm), 2)) |> arrange(desc(total_tpm)) set.seed(params$seed) kegg_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v) spearman_perm(kegg_z, env_model[[v]]) |> mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |> rename(kegg = feature) |> mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")) |> left_join(select(kegg_support, kegg, description, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm), by = "kegg") |> mutate(direction = if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"), significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |> arrange(q_bh) message(glue::glue( "{round(100 * mapped_tpm / sum(vent_ko_tpm$scaledTPM), 1)}% of vent KO TPM maps to a KEGG level-B category; ", "{sum(kegg_gradient$significant)} of {nrow(kegg_gradient)} tests clear BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}")) ``` ::: ### Result ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # flag it if a re-run moves the top COG hit away from the one this section describes top_cog <- slice_min(cog_gradient, q_bh, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) if (top_cog$cog != FOCUS_COG || top_cog$variable != FOCUS_VAR) { warning("Top COG association is now ", top_cog$cog, " vs ", top_cog$variable, ", not ", FOCUS_COG, " vs ", FOCUS_VAR, ". At 13 vent units a single-feature test has almost no power, and the one feature that survived family-wise correction could not support an interpretation. 06 takes the same vent units and asks the taxon-level question with more data behind each claim: how broadly across vent-associated taxa each KO is expressed, and whether the curated heterotrophy KOs sit at the lineage-restricted or the broadly shared end of that distribution. ## Summary of all tables `env_vent`: summary of environmental variables we have vs. not.
